Upper limit before triggering a warning in the logs that config files are being thrashed. 
This happens when mods like ConfigWatcher are spamming IO operations and constantly reloading config files.
You really should investigate the cause of any thrashing alerts triggered by this.
It means your config files are being reloaded constantly in the background, that can hurt performance.
A few times is no big deal, but if it's happening constantly, you should investigate the cause.
Set to 0 to disable the alert if you don't care about the performance impact from mods that are repeatedly hammering IO.

When this is enabled dedicated servers will send every peer's ZDO data in the same frame update. However, it will increase server work per frame.
This has no effect on single player games or hosted games.
NOTE: This is similar to the mod "ReturnToSender" You should not use both this feature and that mod at the same time, pick one.
Explanation: The vanilla ZDOMan.SendZDOToPeers2 function splits the sending of ZDO data up over multiple frame updates asynchronously.
That is good if you are playing a hosted game because it will keep your host pc's framerate up when dealing with many peers.
However, a dedicated server runs headless. spreading the zdo updates over multiple frames can cause clients to have packets arriving a bit later than needed.
(vanilla: false)
